source_excerpt: Lot coverage shall apply to R-MF, R-6 (three-family) and all commercial zones.
review_note: The ordinance explicitly limits lot-coverage applicability to R-MF, R-6 three-family, and commercial zones (§6-5(34.1)). RA-4 is not included. Minimum Green Area (84% for RA-4, §6-205) remains auxiliary evidence and is not converted into maximum lot coverage, since §6-5(34.1)'s definition of Lot Coverage includes buildings, parking, driveways, decks, pools, patios, and terraces -- green area is not shown to be its legal complement. (manually reviewed 2026-10-01)

raw_value: On lots used for single-family residence purposes, Short-term Residential Rentals, or for boarding or rooming houses sufficient garage space or outdoor parking space shall be provided to accommodate the passenger cars used by the residents of such premises.
source_excerpt: On lots used for single-family residence purposes, Short-term Residential Rentals, or for boarding or rooming houses sufficient garage space or outdoor parking space shall be provided to accommodate the passenger cars used by the residents of such premises.
review_note: §6-154 (Parking and Garages for Residential Purposes) is the controlling single-family residential parking provision for RA-4. It imposes a qualitative sufficiency requirement rather than a numeric minimum expressed as spaces per dwelling unit. Numeric parking schedules found elsewhere (§6-155: 1-1.6 spaces/bedroom for two-family/multi-family; §6-121: BMR units) apply to different uses and are not substituted for the RA-4 principal single-family rule. (manually reviewed 2026-10-01)

source_excerpt: The following principal uses are permitted in RA-4, RA-2, RA-1, R-20 and R-12 Zones and all other principal uses are expressly excluded: (1) Detached single family dwellings, one (1) per lot.
review_note: Greenwich defines a multi-family dwelling (§6-5(19)) as a building containing three or more dwelling units. Multifamily housing is not among the enumerated RA-4 principal uses, and §6-93 expressly excludes all other principal uses. Therefore multifamily housing with three or more dwelling units is prohibited as a principal use in RA-4. (manually reviewed 2026-10-01)

review_note: §6-99 expressly includes RA-4 among its named eligible zones (also for the 1,200 sq ft external-ADU size cap under RA-2/RA-4). A conforming ADU is allowed subject to objective standards (owner occupancy, size limits, lot/setback conformance, parking, utility/septic documentation) and staff-level Planning and Zoning Office / Town Planner or designee approval -- not Commission discretionary review. Special Permit / Commission review applies only to the exception case (oversized ADU or nonconforming lot per §6-99(3)(E)), not the ordinary conforming pathway. (manually reviewed 2026-10-01)
